why: One lookup. Orchestrate mode must spawn exactly one worker and relay a sourced figure; classic mode must fetch the page, not quote a snippet.
text: What does 1 kg of carrots (gulerødder) cost in a Danish supermarket right now? Give the price in DKK and the URL of the page you got it from.

why: No research at all — a pure build+deliver task. Measures whether the orchestrator wastes workers on it and whether the file gets built by script and verified.
text: Create an Excel file savings.xlsx with a 12-month savings plan: start with 5000 DKK, deposit 1500 DKK at the start of every month, 3% yearly interest compounded monthly on the balance. Columns: month, deposit, interest, balance. Send me the file.

why: Three independent targets → three workers in parallel, one CSV assembled from their files. The canonical fan-out case.
text: Compare the current monthly price in Denmark of Netflix (standard plan), Disney+ (standard plan) and HBO Max (standard plan). Deliver a CSV file with columns: service, plan, price_dkk, source_url. Send me the file.

why: The run that motivated this work: Danish prices for three items, comparison across shops, an Excel budget for 220 people with sources. Failed on a small model by marking research done with no data and delivering an empty workbook.
text: Lav et budget for 220 personer til en fest med pulled pork burger, coleslaw og hjemmelavet ovn kartofler. Find danske priser på ingredienserne (pulled pork/nakkefilet, burgerboller, coleslaw-ingredienser, kartofler), sammenlign priser fra forskellige butikker, og lav et Excel-ark med budgettet. Angiv kilder til alle priser i arket. Send mig arket.

why: A Danish-language single fact with a source. Checks locale handling through a worker and that the answer reaches the user in Danish with a URL.
text: Hvad er indbyggertallet i Aarhus Kommune ifølge de nyeste tal? Skriv tallet og hvor du fandt det (link).
